key_insight: μ-Bench evaluates whether a voice agent can complete interconnected tasks for multiple people sharing a conversation while respecting each person’s authority, privacy, and constraints. Simulated participants react throughout the session rather than following a fixed script.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations provide limited coverage of dynamic, shared-space conversations where multiple users have different goals and permissions and respond to the agent’s actions.
method: Benchmark joint task completion through closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction.
Give simulated participants isolated profiles containing individual goals, knowledge, and permissions.
Let participants adapt to the agent’s speech and tool outcomes as the interaction unfolds.
impact: μ-Bench offers practitioners a way to evaluate voice assistants under dynamic multi-user demands, not just isolated requests. The provided abstract is incomplete, so no quantitative results or demonstrated performance gains can be reported.
visual_elements: A shared-space diagram showing several users interacting with one voice agent.
A feedback-loop diagram linking agent speech, tool outcomes, and participant reactions.
Individual profile cards with icons for goals, knowledge, permissions, and privacy.
A conversation timeline with overlapping speech and interdependent task milestones.
paper_title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
paper_authors: Qihao Lin, Guanxu Chen, Shuhang Zheng, Xiaoya Lu, Jingyi Yang
